lessons.title: Working on the pork slaughter line
lessons.html:
Your work experience on the line

This is the biggest work experience module in the Pork Slaughterer qualification. You spend many weeks on a real pork slaughter line, working at each station under a mentor. You must show that you can do each process to the abattoir's standard, at line speed, safely and hygienically.

Stations you will work at

  1. Stunning (only once you are trained and authorised)
  2. Shackling, sticking and bleeding
  3. Scalding and de-hairing
  4. Gambrelling and hoisting
  5. Singeing, scraping and shaving
  6. Bunging and opening the belly
  7. Evisceration: rough offal and pluck
  8. Presenting the carcass, head and organs for inspection
  9. Splitting (trained and authorised workers only)
  10. Trimming, washing, weighing and chilling

You usually start at the easier stations, such as shaving and washing, and move to the more skilled ones as your mentor sees you are ready.

Line speed and quality

The line moves at a set speed. At first you will be slow. That is normal. Focus on doing the job correctly; speed comes with practice. Never take shortcuts to keep up. If you fall behind, tell your team leader. It is better to slow the line than to send out a dirty or badly dressed carcass.

Respect the pig

Humane handling applies on the line too. Every pig must be properly stunned before sticking. If you see a pig that is not properly stunned, call out at once so that it is re-stunned.

lessons.title: Safety and hygiene at every station
lessons.html:
Knife safety

  • Keep knives sharp. A blunt knife needs more force and slips.
  • Steel your knife often during the shift and have it sharpened as the plant arranges.
  • Always cut away from your body and your other hand.
  • Wear your cut-resistant glove and chain-mail apron if provided.
  • Never try to catch a falling knife. Step back and let it fall.
  • Carry knives in a scabbard, never in your hand while walking.

Machine safety

  • Only use machines you are trained and authorised for: stunner, de-hairer, splitting saw, hoists.
  • Never reach into a running machine.
  • Know where the emergency stops are.
  • Report damaged guards, cables or hoses.

Hygiene at each station

  • Sterilise your knife between carcasses and when it touches anything dirty.
  • Wash hands often, especially after touching the hide, guts or the floor.
  • Keep carcasses off the floor and away from walls.
  • Stay in your area, dirty or clean, and follow the crossing rules.

Your body

Repetitive cutting can hurt your wrists, shoulders and back. Use the work-stand height that fits you, use sharp knives, and do the stretches your plant shows you. Report pain early; it is easier to treat.

Injuries

Report every cut or injury, even a small one, to your supervisor. Get first aid from a trained first aider. Cuts must be covered before you go back to work, and a deep cut needs medical care. First aid must be learned in hands-on training by an accredited provider.

lessons.title: Assessment and your portfolio of evidence
lessons.html:
How you are assessed

Your mentor watches you at each station on many days. For each process the mentor checks that you:

  • Follow the abattoir's procedure in the right order.
  • Work hygienically and sterilise your tools.
  • Work safely and use protective equipment.
  • Produce a carcass that meets the standard: clean, hair-free, no gut contamination, correctly split and trimmed.
  • Keep up with the line, or ask for help in time.
  • Follow the meat inspector's instructions.

Your portfolio

Keep a logbook showing:

  • Each station you worked at, the dates, and the number of carcasses you did.
  • Your mentor's comments and signature for each station.
  • Mistakes you made and what you learned, for example a gut cut and how you changed your technique.
  • Any incidents and how they were handled.

Learning from mistakes

Everyone makes mistakes when learning. What matters is that you report the mistake, help fix it and learn. Hiding a gut cut or a dirty carcass puts consumers at risk and is a serious offence.

The end goal

When you finish, you should be able to work at any station on the pork line, know why each step matters, and help train new workers. This also prepares you for the external assessment for the qualification.

Key points

  • Work at every station on the pork line under a mentor, starting with easier ones.
  • Do the job correctly first; speed comes with practice.
  • Use sharp knives, cut away from your body and never reach into running machines.
  • Sterilise knives between carcasses and keep carcasses off the floor.
  • Report mistakes and injuries, and keep your logbook signed and honest.
